Good afternoon, and welcome to this session of the infrastructure committee. Before we hear from our witnesses, a few rules. Each witness has three minutes for an opening statement. Three minutes, not four. If you go over, I will stop you, politely but firmly, and your full written statement will still be part of the record. After the statements, each member of the committee has five minutes for questions. Members, please ask questions, not speeches. And one request to our witnesses: for every number you give us today, please tell us where it comes from. This committee has heard many numbers over the years, and not all of them were real. Our first witness is an expert on port concessions. You have three minutes.

I have testified before committees about forty times, and I have three rules. The first is about numbers. Never guess. If a member asks you for a number and you do not know it, say: I do not have the exact figure, and I will send it to the committee in writing. Nobody has ever lost credibility by saying that. Many people have lost it by guessing. The second rule is about mistakes. You will make one. When you do, correct it immediately, in one sentence, and continue. A quick correction makes you look more careful, not less. The third rule is about loaded questions, the ones like: so you admit that the policy failed? Do not say yes, and do not say no. Name the assumption, calmly: that question assumes the policy failed. Then answer the real issue. It works almost every time.
